html:
On 13 May 1888 Brazil abolished slavery with the Golden Law, signed by Princess Isabel, who was ruling while her father, Emperor Pedro II, was abroad. Brazil was the last country in the Americas to end slavery.

Brazil had received more enslaved Africans than any other country, about 40 per cent of all those carried in the Atlantic slave trade. Enslaved people had long resisted, from Palmares onward. Abolition came step by step:

  • 1850: the import of enslaved people was banned.
  • 1871: children born to enslaved mothers were declared free.
  • 1885: enslaved people over sixty were freed.
  • 1880s: abolitionists such as Joaquim Nabuco campaigned, and enslaved people fled the coffee plantations in large numbers.

The law itself had just two short articles. It freed about 700,000 people, with no payment to owners and no land or help for the freed. Angry planters dropped their support for the monarchy, and in 1889 the army overthrew the emperor and declared a republic.
sum: On 13 May 1888 Brazil abolished slavery with the Golden Law, signed by Princess Isabel, who was ruling while her father, Emperor Pedro II, was abroad. Brazil was the last country in the Americas to end slavery.
